item.title: Clinical and radiological comparisons of posterior labral tears with and without posterior glenohumeral instability
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Clinical and magnetic resonance findings of posterior labral tears without glenohumeral instability differ from those with instability. Surgical treatment achieved satisfactory clinical outcomes regardless of the presence of instability. Level of evidence: III.

item.title: From Genes to Neural Circuits: Genetic and Systems Mechanisms of Ethanol Sensitivity and Tolerance in Drosophila melanogaster
item.description: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a complex neuropsychiatric disease shaped by genetic, environmental, and physiological factors. Over four decades, Drosophila melanogaster has emerged as a powerful model for dissecting the molecular and neural mechanisms underlying ethanol sensitivity, tolerance, preference, and consumption. Its conserved signaling pathways, sophisticated genetic toolkit, and robust behavioral assays have enabled discovery of genes and neural circuits governing alcohol responses...

item.title: Plant cytokinin ortho-topolin riboside suppresses the proliferation of multiple myeloma cells by promoting β-catenin degradation
item.description: Multiple myeloma involves the aberrant activation of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway, resulting in β-catenin accumulation. Targeting this pathway presents a promising therapeutic approach for multiple myeloma. A cell-based chemical assay revealed that ortho-topolin riboside (oTR), a cytokinin naturally produced by Populus robusta, effectively suppressed the activation of β-catenin response transcription induced by Wnt3aconditioned medium. The mechanism underlying this suppression involved...

item.title: 8-Chloro-cyclic AMP mediates growth inhibition of breast cancer cells via regulation of Yin-Yang 1 and estrogen receptor α levels
item.description: As a derivative of cyclic AMP (cAMP), 8-Chloro-cyclic AMP (8-Cl-cAMP) is shown to induce growth inhibition, apoptosis, and differentiation in different cancer cells by activating AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and p38 mitogen-activated protein kinase (p38 MAPK). The p38 MAPK is known as a downstream mediator of 8-Cl-cAMP and binds to a multifunctional transcription factor Yin-Yang 1 (YY1). Although cytotoxic effects of 8-Cl-cAMP on cancer cells have been studied over several decades,...

item.title: Premature Occlusal Contacts Induce MRONJ in Osseointegrated Dental Implants: An Experimental In Vivo Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that POC contributes to peri-implant osteonecrosis under ZOL treatment, supporting occlusal trauma as an important local factor in MRONJ development around osseointegrated dental implants.

item.title: Utilization of serum vitamin A testing and vitamin A deficiency in Korea
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Although vitamin A deficiency does not represent a major public health burden in Korea, older adults and specific high-risk groups may be vulnerable. These findings provide a real-world overview of vitamin A testing practices and support targeted clinical and nutritional assessment in selected populations.

item.title: Total and beverage-specific alcohol use at mid-life and all-cause and cause-specific mortality: a prospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The results suggested that low to moderate alcohol intake from spirits and beer/cider was associated with higher all-cause, CVD, cancer, and other mortality, whereas low to moderate alcohol use from wine was associated with lower all-cause, CVD, cancer, and other mortality. However, high alcohol use, regardless of beverage-type, mortality from various site-specific cancers was elevated.

item.title: Prognostic factors associated with outcomes after knee cartilage repair across different procedure types: a systematic review
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Available evidence identifies candidate prognostic associations within specific disease, procedure, outcome, and follow-up contexts. However, substantial clinical heterogeneity, potential confounding, cohort overlap, and sparse context-specific evidence limit the certainty and generalizability of the findings. The evidence does not support universal clinical cutoffs or conclusions that prognostic effects differ between procedures.

item.title: The efficacy of psychological interventions for anxiety in Parkinson's disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis including mindfulness and mind-body approaches
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Psychological and mind-body interventions may reduce anxiety symptoms in individuals with PD, and a similar reduction was observed at follow-up. However, the clinical interpretation of this effect requires caution because different anxiety scales were used across trials, the number of included studies was limited, several studies were rated as having a high risk of bias, the prediction interval included the null, and the effect derives principally from comparisons with inactive...

item.title: Proteomic analysis of transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation induced cognitive restoration in a mouse model of vascular cognitive impairment
item.description: Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) is a major cause of dementia with limited treatment options. Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) is a noninvasive neuromodulation approach that has shown cognitive benefits, but its molecular basis remains unclear. Here, we employed a mouse model of transient bilateral common carotid artery occlusion (tBCCAO) to identify molecular candidates underlying the cognitive restorative effects of taVNS. tBCCAO impaired cognitive function as...

item.title: Optimization of <sup>68</sup>Ga-lactosylated human serum albumin (LSA) for PET-based quantitative evaluation of hepatic functional reserve in liver fibrosis models
item.description: Accurate preoperative assessment of hepatic functional reserve (HFR) and future remnant liver function is essential for reducing postoperative morbidity and mortality after liver surgery, yet current clinical methods remain indirect and provide limited spatial and quantitative information. Here, we developed an asialoglycoprotein receptor (ASGPR)-targeted tracer for positron emission tomography (PET), [^(68)Ga]Ga-NOTA-lactosylated human serum albumin ([^(68)Ga]Ga-NOTA-LSA), and systematically...

item.title: Prevalence of Y93H resistance-associated substitution in treatment-naïve hepatitis C virus genotype 1b patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: The Y93H substitution is a frequent naturally occurring variant in untreated HCV genotype 1b infection. Despite reduced clinical relevance with pangenotypic DAAs, its persistence warrants continued monitoring. Standardized sequencing and global resistance surveillance remain essential for optimizing treatment strategies and informing antiviral policy.

item.title: Large-scale GWAS integrated with image-based phenotyping reveals loci and trait-associated markers for Perilla frutescens seed traits
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study represents the first large-scale GWAS integrating image-based phenotyping for seed traits in perilla and provides candidate dCAPS markers with potential applicability to marker-assisted selection, pending validation in independent breeding populations. These findings offer valuable genetic resources and a practical framework for molecular breeding and crop improvement in perilla.

item.title: Impact of neck nodal yield on immune checkpoint inhibitor outcome after recurrence in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Extensive lymphatic ablation, as reflected by high LNY, may be associated with diminished ICI efficacy in relapsed HNSCC. These findings suggest that LNY warrants further investigation as a potential biomarker for ICI outcomes in patients with post-surgical recurrent HNSCC.

item.title: Chiral-Nematic Lattice Instability in Charge Density Wave of 1T-TiSe<sub>2</sub>
item.description: Chiral charge-density waves (CDWs) are a rare form of electronic order with handedness, enabling novel couplings among light, lattice, and topology in quantum materials. Yet the microscopic origin of chirality has remained elusive, even in the prototypical chiral CDW system 1T-TiSe(2). Using ab initio calculations, we investigate the structural stability and electronic structure of competing CDW models in 1T-TiSe(2). We show that a chiral monoclinic ( C 2 ) structure is stabilized by the...

item.title: Response to the Letter to the Editor Regarding "Does Surgeon Experience Influence Surgical Safety and Patient Satisfaction After Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion? A Prospective Multicenter Comparison Study Between Non-Board-Certified and Board-Certified Spine Surgeons"
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Site-Selective Initial Hydration of Boron at Multicomponent Borosilicate Glass-Water Interfaces Revealed Using Machine Learning Molecular Dynamics
item.description: Understanding the hydration reactions at borosilicate glass-water interfaces is essential for predicting long-term chemical durability. However, atomistic simulations of multicomponent glass corrosion require both chemical accuracy and nanosecond-scale sampling, which remain difficult to achieve using conventional force fields or ab initio molecular dynamics. This paper describes the development and validation of a machine learning potential (MLP) for multicomponent borosilicate glass-water...

item.title: Nanoengineered STING agonists for cancer therapy: toward immunodynamic control
item.description: Activation of the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes (cGAS-STING) pathway is a mechanistically compelling strategy for cancer immunotherapy, but first-generation STING agonists have shown limited clinical activity despite clear pharmacodynamic induction of interferon-related signals. This translational gap suggests that therapeutic benefit depends not only on pathway engagement but also on where, in which cells, at what amplitude, and for how long STING is activated. In this...

item.title: Severe perioperative immune-related adverse events requiring intensive care in patients with gastric cancer: a case series
item.description: CONCLUSION: As immune checkpoint inhibitors are increasingly incorporated into multidisciplinary treatment for gastric cancer, surgeons may encounter severe perioperative immune-related adverse events requiring intensive care management. Awareness of these presentations and prompt multidisciplinary management may help facilitate early recognition and appropriate treatment.

item.title: Comprehensive behavioral phenotyping of male Sulf1-deficient mice reveals reduced locomotor activity, altered forelimb gait, and reduced prepulse inhibition
item.description: Sulfatase 1 (Sulf1) is an extracellular sulfatase that regulates multiple signaling pathways by removing 6-O-sulfate from heparan sulfate. Although Sulf1 has established roles in development and cancer, its functions in the adult brain remain incompletely characterized. Recently we reported that Sulf1 is expressed in the nucleus accumbens, overlapping with dopamine D1 and D2 receptors, and that Sulf1 knockout (KO) mice showed altered reward and aversion learning. However, given that Sulf1 is...

item.title: Human chorionic gonadotropin levels of cesarean scar pregnancy compared with those of other ectopic pregnancies: a retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Serum hCG levels in early pregnancy were higher in CSP than in other ectopic pregnancies. Even in the presence of high serum hCG levels during early pregnancy, CSP should be considered if there is a history of cesarean section, especially > 2 cesarean deliveries. The study included only five CSP cases, one of which was a duplicate case from a different treatment cycle. Consequently, the findings should be considered exploratory. Given the limited sample size, additional cases should...

item.title: Incident location at home and emergency medical services on-scene time for older adults in Japan: a population-based cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Higher floors and confined areas (toilets and bathrooms) were associated with longer on-scene time. Future studies are invited to examine the effect of patients' consciousness levels to ensure that paramedics can rapidly reach and transport emergency patients regardless of location.

item.title: Comparison of Labeled Dosages Between Japan and the United States for Drugs Approved in Japan from 2020 to 2025
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 20% of drugs approved in Japan during 2020-2025 had dosage differences from those in the US. The proportion of drugs with dosage differences varied across therapeutic areas. Only 3.7% had major differences. These findings may reflect progress in the international harmonization of labeled drug dosages between Japan and the US.

item.title: Patient characteristics and the safety of stent placement for malignant vena cava syndrome in Japan: a nationwide analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: Stent placement for malignant vena cava obstruction demonstrated an overall complication rate of 10.6% with no serious adverse events requiring invasive intervention.

item.title: Eucalyptus camaldulensis essential oil inhibits biofilm formation and disrupts pre-formed biofilms in clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa: an in vitro study
item.description: CONCLUSION: These in vitro findings suggest that EUEO may be a candidate natural agent against P. aeruginosa biofilms, although viability-based and in vivo studies are needed to confirm this.

item.title: Study protocol of a prospective, non-interventional cohort study evaluating the benefits of transjugular intrahepatic portosystemic shunt in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma receiving first-line atezolizumab plus bevacizumab (NISTIPS TRITICC-4, IKF092)
item.description: BACKGROUND: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with most patients diagnosed at an advanced stage. Atezolizumab plus bevacizumab is a current standard first-line therapy; however, outcomes are strongly influenced by underlying cirrhosis and clinically significant portal hypertension (CSPH). Complications such as ascites and variceal bleeding may limit treatment continuation, particularly as bevacizumab increases bleeding risk. Transjugular intrahepatic...

item.title: Wheat TaHGH1/HSFA2D integrates temperature and gravity signals to control starch granule biogenesis and auxin asymmetry for shaping shoot architecture plasticity
item.description: Shoot architecture, mainly determined by tiller angle, is a key agronomic trait affecting crop yield. Winter wheat undergoes dynamic erect-prostrate growth transitions in response to low temperatures during overwintering, yet the coordinated regulation of shoot architecture by temperature and gravity remains elusive. In this study, we identified TaHGH1, an HSFA2 transcription factor, via GWAS and found it positively regulates shoot gravitropism and thereby reduces tiller angle. TaHGH1 promotes...

item.title: Climate-driven redistribution of Hyalomma marginatum (Ixodida: Ixodidae): robust ecological niche modeling reveals future expansion and quantifies projection uncertainty
item.description: Hyalomma marginatum (Ixodida: Ixodidae) is the principal vector of Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) and an emerging public health concern because climate change may facilitate its establishment in regions where it is currently absent. We used ecological niche modeling to characterize the current climatic suitability of H. marginatum and project its future redistribution across the Old World under CMIP6 climate scenarios. Models were calibrated using a comprehensive dataset of...

item.title: Association between IRAK1 gene rs1059703 polymorphism and rheumatoid arthritis risk
item.description: CONCLUSION: A statistically significant association between IRAK1 rs1059703 and RA risk was observed in Caucasian populations, but not in Asian populations with the available power under the current sample size. The apparent Caucasian association observed in the full dataset was not sustained after restricting analyses to HWE-compliant studies, where only a single Caucasian study remained.

item.title: Dysregulation of the miR-29c-3p/collagen axis induces spermatogenic failure in heat stress and non-obstructive azoospermia
item.description: Rising global temperatures have intensified male infertility linked to testicular heat stress. While microRNAs play pivotal roles in spermatogenesis, the reason for aberrant microRNA expression following heat stress-induced spermatogenic disorders remains largely unclear. We established a murine heat stress model and performed small RNA sequencing. Candidate microRNAs were obtained via intersection with additional spermatogenic arrest and Sertoli cell-only syndrome datasets. The proliferation of...

item.title: Abscopal effect-induced acephalic spermatozoa and testicular dysfunction implicate Cep112 and PI3K/Akt-mTOR signaling
item.description: The abscopal effect, a systemic phenomenon induced by localized irradiation and associated with inflammatory factor activation, has attracted significant interest in the context of radiotherapy combined with immunotherapy. While recognized as potentially beneficial in oncology, this effect can have detrimental off-target consequences. The underlying mechanisms for abscopal effect-induced testicular dysfunction remain unclear. In this study, we observed a pronounced testicular disruption...

item.title: Tropical leaf phenology as a thermoregulation trait: how changes in crown structure modulate thermal dynamics for two dominant Hawaiian trees
item.description: Canopy and leaf temperatures often diverge from air temperature, influencing photosynthesis, water loss, and heat stress. While leaf traits are known to affect heat exchange, how changes in crown structure interact with environmental drivers to regulate canopy thermal dynamics is poorly understood, particularly in tropical forests. In a Hawaiian wet tropical montane forest, we used repeated UAV-based (Unmanned Aerial Vehicle) thermal and LiDAR (light detection and ranging) measurements of sunlit...

item.title: Skyrmion Bubbles by Design in a Centrosymmetric Kagome Magnet
item.description: Topologically protected nanoscale spin textures, such as magnetic skyrmions, have attracted significant interest for spintronics applications. While skyrmions in noncentrosymmetric materials are known to be stabilized by the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), their deliberate design in centrosymmetric materials remains a challenge. This difficulty largely stems from the complexity of controlling magnetocrystalline anisotropy-a critical factor in the absence of DMI. Here, we demonstrate the...

item.title: EXPRESS: Quantification of arterial hemodynamics in steno-occlusive disease using time-resolved MRI-based angiography
item.description: BackgroundIntracranial steno-occlusive disease (SOD) assessment benefits from hemodynamic imaging, but comprehensive evaluation often relies on contrast- or radiation-based techniques. Arterial spin labeling (ASL) provides a non-invasive alternative for quantifying tissue-level perfusion and cerebrovascular reactivity, yet does not capture upstream arterial flow dynamics. As a result, non-invasive assessment of macrovascular hemodynamics for SOD remains limited. This study evaluates whether...

item.title: Anion-Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
item.description: Anion-dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low-temperature sodium-metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature-sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion-cation-targeted regulation via Sn(OTf)(2) that simultaneously constructs a solvent-reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy-based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na(15)Sn(4)), which goes beyond the...

item.title: Dual-Targeting Nanomicelles Co-Loading Sorafenib and Artesunate Combats Hepatocellular Carcinoma via the Synergistically Enhanced Ferroptosis Strategy
item.description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a formidable malignancy with limited response to conventional monotherapies, largely due to its complicated pathogenesis and useful cellular defense systems. In this study, we constructed a dual-targeting polymeric micelle (S&A@TPD/HG PMs), co-delivering sorafenib (SOR), and artesunate (ART) to achieve synergistic ferroptosis-based therapy against HCC. The micelle features a hyaluronic acid (HA) shell functionalized with glycyrrhetinic acid (GA) for active...

item.title: NEK2 Promotes OSCC Invasion and Metastasis by Activating TNF-α Signaling Through Impairment of Desmosomal Adhesion
item.description: NIMA-related kinase 2 (NEK2) is a cell cycle regulator aberrantly overexpressed in multiple cancers, yet its non-mitotic roles in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) invasion and metastasis remain unclear. Here, we analyzed public transcriptomic and single-cell datasets and found that NEK2 is significantly upregulated in OSCC tissues, with higher expression in cases exhibiting lymph node metastasis and associations with poor prognosis. Functional assays demonstrated that NEK2 promotes OSCC cell...

item.title: Eosinophilic Oesophagitis and Incidence of Gastrointestinal Cancer: A Population-Based Cohort Study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: One year after EoE diagnosis, oesophageal cancer and hepatocellular carcinoma rates remained elevated. Most oesophageal cancers occurred in patients with prior BE, suggesting that the association between EoE and oesophageal cancer may be mediated largely through BE.

item.title: Letter: Diagnostic Assessment and Temporal Trends in Non-Helicobacter pylori, Non-NSAID Bleeding Ulcers
item.description: No abstract

item.title: Whole-blood transcriptomic findings in emergency department patients with suspected cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome: a pilot study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Together, these preliminary findings identify immune-related signals in ED patients with suspected CHS, and lay the groundwork for future studies with larger, prospectively phenotyped cohorts to identify biomarkers, clarify immune triggers, and develop targeted therapies.

item.title: Spatiotemporal plasticity of the gut microbiome facilitates redbelly tilapia (Coptodon zillii) invasion in China
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The gut microbiome of invasive C. zillii displays significant spatiotemporal variation in structure, diversity, and functional gene composition. This pronounced plasticity-rather than a stable, specialized microbiota-likely serves as a key adaptive strategy, enabling the species to thrive in heterogeneous environments.

item.title: Capsaicin suppresses microglial inflammation through TRPV1-SSR4 interaction
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Our findings suggest that capsaicin suppresses microglial inflammation mediated by the TRPV1-SSR4 interaction, providing new insights into the chemical biology basis of TRPV1 interoceptive signaling and potential applications of natural TRPV1 agonists for modifying therapy of neuroinflammation-associated neurodegeneration.

item.title: Motor network neurophysiological (TMS-EEG) markers as predictors of outcomes of ventriculoperitoneal shunt sustained for over a year in normal pressure hydrocephalus
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study indicates that higher M1L WFA obtained through Delphi-MD (TMS-EEG), signifies better preservation and functional integrity of the motor network in patients with probable iNPH that had a sustained response to VPS than those that did not. Given replication of results in future independent cohorts, Delphi-MD shows promise as an objective, accurate, and accessible ancillary screening tool for iNPH candidates, prior to referral for VPS treatment.

item.title: ABCD-Trial: study protocol for a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study in patients with Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis for the evaluation of efficacy and safety of B-Cell Depletion with rituximab (ABCD)
item.description: BACKGROUND: The exact disease-causing mechanisms in ALS remain incompletely understood. A possible cause is inflammation of neurons. Compared to other neurodegenerative diseases, neuroinflammation is pronounced in ALS, presumably leading to disease progression and neuronal death. Patients with ALS can have neuronal autoantibodies and most notably antibody-producing cells in the cerebrospinal fluid. The CD20-binding therapeutic antibody rituximab targets these antibody-producing B-cells....

item.title: StitchR-based dual-AAV delivery strategies enable efficient transduction of defined neural cell populations
item.description: Dual adeno-associated virus (AAV) vector reconstitution has become an indispensable technique for delivering large genes in neuroscience and gene therapy. A novel technology termed StitchR addresses the challenge of low efficiency in dual-AAV reconstruction, yet related tools enabling targeted gene delivery to specific neural cell populations remain insufficiently developed. Herein, we developed four StitchR-based dual-viral reconstitution strategies by combining high-efficiency AAV serotypes...

item.title: ASH2L-mediated H3K4me3 methylation governs palatal development by regulating WNT5B
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings establish ASH2L-mediated H3K4me3 as a critical epigenetic regulator of palatal development through WNT5B modulation, and identify potential therapeutic targets for cleft palate.

item.title: Parkinson's disease LRRK2 mutations dysregulate iron homeostasis and promote oxidative stress and ferroptosis in human neurons and astrocytes
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Together, our findings show that pathogenic LRRK2 mutations converge on disrupted iron homeostasis across multiple human neural cell types, including dopaminergic neurons, and support a link between LRRK2 signaling, lysosomal iron dysregulation and ferroptosis-related stress.

item.title: P4HA1⁺ collagen-modifying fibroblasts are associated with pro-tumor niches and therapeutic vulnerabilities in colorectal cancer
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: This study characterizes a P4HA1⁺ collagen-modifying CAF subpopulation that resides within a spatially organized multicellular niche and engages distinct signaling axes to simultaneously promote angiogenesis, immune suppression, and tumor cell proliferation in CRC, highlighting its prognostic and potential therapeutic value.

item.title: Identification of a putative founder variant in SLC30A10 associated with hypermanganesemia with dystonia 1 in Iranian patients: a case series and literature review
item.description: Hypermanganesemia with dystonia 1 (HMNDYT1) is an rare autosomal recessive condition resulting from pathogenic variants in the SLC30A10 gene. The presence of biallelic variants in this gene results in systemic accumulation of manganese, which leads to dystonia, polycythemia, and liver dysfunction. We conducted clinical and genetic evaluations of seven affected individuals from six Iranian consanguineous families, emphasizing the identification of potential founder mutations, and integrated this...

item.title: AI-guided design and biomaterial integration for next-generation extracellular vesicle therapeutics: an evidence-weighted translational framework
item.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are promising therapeutic and diagnostic platforms, yet their clinical translation remains constrained by population heterogeneity, limited target-site retention, uncertain biodistribution, and variable potency. These persistent limitations have motivated the convergence of artificial intelligence (AI), biomaterials, synthetic biology, and advanced validation systems into what we describe as a next-generation EV framework. The evidence supporting these enabling...

item.title: Mapping and analysis of the knowledge graph on the current status and key issues in global research on Norovirus infections in children over the past 28 years
item.description: CONCLUSION: Global research on NoV infections in children has evolved into a Multi-Disciplinary research framework driven by virology, epidemiology, clinical medicine, and public health. Current research focuses primarily on molecular epidemiology and genetic diversity, as well as epidemiological characteristics and outbreak transmission mechanisms, while the assessment of disease burden and the optimization of global prevention and control strategies are gradually emerging as key future...

item.title: Multiscale epidemiology of gastrointestinal nematode infections in small ruminants: field evidence from Inner Mongolia and a national meta-analysis in China
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The findings demonstrate marked local variation in GIN prevalence in the regional survey and substantial descriptive spatial variation across the provincial-level estimates included in the national meta-analysis. The regional microscopy-based survey supports broad egg-category inference but not reliable genus- or species-level identification of non-Nematodirus strongylid nematodes. These results support geographically targeted surveillance and locally adapted parasite-control...

item.title: Stroke-associated pneumonia: from immunodepression to bedside management and future research directions
item.description: Stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) is one of the most frequent complications after acute stroke, affecting approximately one in eight stroke patients. Besides prolonged hospitalisation and increased healthcare costs, it is also a major risk factor for mortality and poor functional recovery. The pathophysiology of SAP is driven by two converging processes: impaired local airway defence due to dysphagia as well as reduced airway clearance reflexes, and systemic stroke-induced immunodepression...

item.title: Blocking IL-6 trans-signaling mitigates benzalkonium chloride-induced inflammation, oxidative imbalance, ER stress, and barrier disruption in human corneal epithelial cells
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings indicate that IL-6 trans-signaling contributes to BAC-induced corneal epithelial injury, suggesting that targeting this pathway may have therapeutic potential for DED and related ocular surface inflammatory disorders.

item.title: Cobimetinib impairs tumor survival and immune escape by altering my-CAFs in BRAFV600E-mutated anaplastic thyroid carcinoma
item.description: Anaplastic thyroid carcinoma is one of the most aggressive thyroid cancers characterized by rapid progression and high resistance to conventional therapies. Although mutations in the BRAF gene are common in thyroid cancer, targeted therapies against this mutation show limited clinical benefit. This study investigated whether inhibition of downstream signaling pathways using the selected MEK inhibitor cobimetinib provides advantages over direct BRAF inhibition. Genomic and expression analyses of...

item.title: Multidomain Autonomic Dysfunction assessed with COMPASS-31 among patients with type 2 diabetes in Zanzibar: prevalence and associated factors
item.description: CONCLUSION: Approximately half of the adults with T2DM in this tertiary-care population had COMPASS-31-defined autonomic dysfunction. Higher prevalence was associated with no family history of diabetes, longer diabetes duration, non-use of oral hypoglycemic agents, and lower vegetable intake. These findings highlight the potential value of symptom-based autonomic assessment and support further prospective research to better understand the clinical and lifestyle factors associated with autonomic...

item.title: Human papillomavirus awareness and prevention practices among patients with Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome after neovagina reconstruction: a cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Despite relatively high awareness of HPV and its prevention, Chinese patients with MRKH syndrome after neovagina reconstruction showed markedly low uptake of HPV vaccination and limited engagement with HPV testing. These findings highlight an unmet need for accessible HPV vaccination, neovaginal HPV risk education, and tailored sexual health education for this rare and underserved population. Further research is warranted to identify barriers to preventive care and to develop...

item.title: Association of serum uric acid during pre-pregnancy with adverse pregnancy outcomes among women conceived by in-vitro fertilization: a retrospective cohort study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings suggest that optimizing serum UA levels in women planning pregnancy, particularly those undergoing IVF-ET, may have important clinical implications for improving pregnancy outcomes.

item.title: Cancer metastasis: biological mechanisms, therapeutic bottlenecks, and emerging interventions
item.description: Metastatic cancer remains a major clinical challenge, which is driven by the continuous adaptation of disseminated tumor cells to diverse tissue environments and therapeutic pressures. Although current treatments, including conventional therapies, small-molecule drugs, antibody-drug conjugates, and immunotherapies, have improved clinical outcomes in selected patients, they rarely achieve durable disease control, largely because each stage of the metastatic cascade presents distinct therapeutic...

item.title: Postpartum contraception receipt among Oregon Medicaid-funded births with stimulant and substance use disorder
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Birthing people enrolled in Medicaid who misused stimulants were more likely than those without SUD, controlling for relevant factors, to receive postpartum contraception within 60 days due to elevated contraception receipt during the IPP period. Further research may examine whether these findings can be replicated outside of Oregon.

item.title: Sensory impairment, loneliness, and the emergence of physical-psychological-cognitive multimorbidity: a cross-national cohort study in China, the United States, and England
item.description: BACKGROUND: The co-occurrence of physical diseases, psychological disorders, and cognitive impairment-here termed physical-psychological-cognitive multimorbidity (PPC-M)-poses growing challenges to healthy aging but its upstream, modifiable determinants remain underexplored. Sensory impairments are common in later life and may be associated with the emergence of PPC-M, partly through psychosocial factors such as loneliness. This study aimed to examine the associations of vision, hearing, and...

item.title: Efficiency and productivity of Mongolian subnational public hospital systems, 2014-2023: annual DEA, global Malmquist and double-bootstrap analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Mongolian regional public hospital systems showed high contemporaneous technical efficiency but several statistically supported periods of productivity decline, including 2019-2020, followed by recovery in 2020-2021. The revised independent-region analysis does not support a robust regression claim that geographic area predicts inefficiency. DEA results are relative production benchmarks, not cost-effectiveness estimates or incremental cost-effectiveness ratios, and should inform...

item.title: Socioeconomic transitions and the spatial dynamics of syphilis transmission in urbanizing China
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Syphilis transmission in China exhibits clear spatial stratification, where the burden is increasingly shifting to resource-constrained regions. The divergence between consumption-based risk in developed areas and survival-based risk in underdeveloped hinterlands underscores how macroeconomic instability amplifies health inequalities Equity-oriented interventions must prioritize "poverty-driven" transmission pathways and vulnerable older populations to prevent the entrenchment of...

item.title: Deleted in lymphocytic leukemia 2 contributes to lung fibroblast activation and pulmonary fibrosis by interacting with and triggering focal adhesion kinase phosphorylation
item.description: The etiology of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unknown, and therapeutic interventions are currently restricted. The activation of lung fibroblasts and the focal adhesion kinase (FAK) signaling pathway are crucial to the pathogenesis of IPF, yet the exact molecular mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Our study shows that the deleted in lymphocytic leukemia 2 (DLEU2) is elevated in the peripheral blood of patients with IPF, as well as in the lung tissues of mice with pulmonary...

item.title: A novel inhalable tanshinone IIA lipid nanocrystal formulation for the enhanced treatment of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
item.description: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive, fatal interstitial lung disease marked by relentless deterioration of pulmonary function. Clinically, oral pharmacotherapy for IPF is hampered by two major limitations: inefficient drug delivery to the lung parenchyma and systemic exposure leading to unavoidable off-target side effects. In this study, we developed an inhalable tanshinone IIA (TA) formulation based on lipid nanocrystals to address these challenges. Leveraging the high drug...

item.title: Neglected tropical diseases in the Arabian Peninsula: a systematic review of leishmaniasis and rickettsioses
item.description: CONCLUSION: Leishmaniasis remains a public health challenge in the Arabian Peninsula, particularly in Saudi Arabia. In contrast, rickettsioses are likely underdiagnosed due to limited surveillance and diagnostic capacity. Improved, integrated surveillance systems, paired with febrile illness investigations that include diagnostic testing for rickettsial pathogens, will lead to fewer missed cases, contributing to disease detection and control.

item.title: Pars plana vitrectomy under air infusion versus conventional fluid infusion for dense vitreous hemorrhage: a retrospective comparative study
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Vitrectomy under air infusion was associated with a shorter effective vitrectomy time than conventional BSS infusion, while achieving comparable short-term visual and anatomical outcomes. The air-vitreous interface may improve intraoperative visualization of hemorrhagic vitreous. As the two techniques produced equivalent short-term outcomes, the potential advantage of air infusion appears to lie in intraoperative efficiency rather than in superior clinical results. Larger...

item.title: Spatial spillover effects and regional differences of tuberculosis health education levels among China's floating population: a spatial lag model study (2014-2017)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The health education regarding tuberculosis among China's floating population demonstrates significant spatial clustering from 2014 to 2017. Key determinants identified include economic factors, healthcare resources, and environmental influences, which contribute not only at a local level but also through notable spatial spillover effects. It is essential to adopt targeted public health strategies to enhance interregional collaboration and optimize resource allocation for equitable...

item.title: Correlation of whole-body fat content and its distribution with lumbar fat content under different age, gender and BMI conditions: quantitative analysis of MRI based on deep learning

item.description: This study examines how nationally representative health survey data can be used to operationalise a life-course approach to health inequalities by examining socioeconomic inequalities and adult obesity in South Korea. item.title: Early Oral Gastrografin Followed by Immediate CT for Precise Leak Localization and Surgical Planning After Total Laryngectomy
item.description: CONCLUSION: Performing CT immediately after an oral Gastrografin swallow significantly improves anatomical localization of pharyngeal leaks following total laryngectomy. By integrating leak detection and anatomical delineation in a single imaging session, this protocol enhances surgical decision-making and may serve as a practical adjunct for postoperative evaluation and management of PCF.

item.description: Cancer immunotherapy has demonstrated remarkable efficacy across multiple tumor types. Despite their significant clinical benefits, most patients with solid tumors remain refractory to immunotherapy, and initial responders frequently develop acquired resistance. item.title: Effective Connectivity and Clinical Correlates in Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
item.description: CONCLUSION: Resting-state VAR-based EC revealed distributed between-group differences in direction-sensitive BOLD temporal organization in COPD. Several of these EC measures were associated with pulmonary function, SpO(2), respiratory and COPD symptom burden, cognition, affect, and health status after age adjustment. These findings extend the functional connectivity profile of COPD by linking directed temporal relationships to its multidimensional clinical burden.

item.title: Pembrolizumab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin for advanced biliary tract cancer: longer-term follow-up from the randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 KEYNOTE-966 trial
item.description: BACKGROUND: At the final analysis of KEYNOTE-966 (median follow-up 25·6 months), pembrolizumab plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (pembrolizumab group) versus placebo plus gemcitabine and cisplatin (placebo group) provided a statistically significant, clinically meaningful improvement in overall survival without any new safety signals in participants with advanced biliary tract cancer. We report results from a median study follow-up of 36·6 months (∼3 years).
